notes: SR6 counts within one program's debugging sections. The Debug module states its rules per program: the ALL PROCEDURES phrase 'can appear only once in a program' (SR7), and the debugging sections are compiled by the WITH DEBUGGING MODE clause of the program that holds them (XV.1.3.3). SR6's purpose is that one reference never requests two debugging sections; in nested programs a declarative is selected first from 'the program that contains the statement which caused the qualifying condition' (X.5.5.4 GR1a), and only a declarative 'in which the GLOBAL phrase is specified' reaches a contained program's statement (GR1b), a phrase USE FOR DEBUGGING does not have (XV.3.2.2). So the outer and the inner USE FOR DEBUGGING ON W-X never compete for one reference: each fires for its own program's statements (e3: OUTER D1 W-X, INNER D1 W-X). Reading SR6 across programs would also make it incoherent for its procedure-name operand, which another program cannot reference at all (IV.4.3.8.1 SRL2.6). Repeats within one program are refused COBOL6335 (the reader's and refuter's probes a6, b8, b9, b10). Leads outside this row, for the records worker: b7a/b7b (RENAMES alias W-R: ON W-R never fires, and MOVE TO W-R fires the W-Y section with DEBUG-NAME 'W-Y') belong to XV.3.2.4 GR6c/GR13; the COBOL6335 text cites 'X3.23-1985 ... syntax rule 6' rather than the §1985 form.
